review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas and no simp-normal-form definitions. The long `attribute [-instance]` and `attribute [-simp]` lines only turn off existing instances and simp rules. The new declarations are `Good` with its closure lemmas, the Galois-fixing lemmas, `T_mem_Gamma1`, and some finiteness and curve statements. None is a natural simp lemma. `Good.mono`, `Good.inter` and `Good.of_forall` are used by explicit application, and tagging them simp would not help. The `simp` calls are local and terminal, for example `simp [ModularGroup.T]` in `T_mem_Gamma1` after `Gamma1_mem`. I found no evidence that these calls have a better normal form or that the file has competing rules or a cycle. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out a simp-set interaction that only shows up at compile time.
